rewrites._comment: Oura Cloud API OAuth2 redirect. Registered at developer.ouraring.com as https://ignia.fit/oura/callback and compared byte-for-byte by Oura, so this path is not free to rename. Without this rewrite hosting serves the SPA shell via the ** rewrite below and the flow dead-ends on a branded 404 that returns 200 — the same failure /open had.

The mobile app's update banner reads this on launch. Since 2026-09-05 it is served from Firestore public/appVersion (refreshed hourly + from /admin), not a static file — there must be NO public/app-version.json, because a static file wins over a rewrite. functions/src/app-version.ts.

headers._comment: Every route. Security headers: framing is SAMEORIGIN (not DENY / 'none') so a same-origin frame keeps working if authDomain ever moves to ignia.fit (Firebase Auth's /__/auth/iframe); today authDomain is the firebaseapp.com host. No script-src CSP on purpose -- Firebase, Sentry and Google sign-in would each need allow-listing and a miss breaks sign-in silently.

A hosting header rule overrides the rewritten function's own Cache-Control (see /oura/callback). This one lets the CDN hold the answer for an hour so the function runs once per edge per hour, not once per app launch; a device sees a new store version within an hour of the sync, which is the sync's own cadence.

Content-hashed build output only (outputHashing: all): scripts, styles, fonts. Unhashed files under these extensions are re-relaxed by the worker rule below -- a later matching rule wins for the same header key.
Images from public/ keep their names across deploys (og-image.png, favicon, icons/*, store badges, hero-mockup), so a year of immutable would pin a stale image in every cache. One day.
Assets Angular copies out of CSS url() references are content-hashed.
Retired-PWA safety workers (ADR-0036): fixed names, must revalidate on every update check so an old install picks up the self-unregistering script.
Same as /ngsw-worker.js; an extglob alternation here did not match on Hosting (verified with curl 2026-10-15).

The `**` rule above sets Cache-Control: no-cache, and a hosting header rule OVERRIDES whatever the rewritten function sets on its own response — so ouraCallback's own no-store was being silently downgraded. no-cache permits STORING the response and only forces revalidation; this URL is reached with an OAuth authorization code in the query string, so it must not be written to disk at all.
Same override problem as /oura/callback: the URL carries the signed unsubscribe token, so the function's own no-store and no-referrer must survive the ** rules above.
